install.title: Install an agent
install.versions: The server hands out sard-agent {{agent}} with restic {{restic}}.
install.noSteps: The release has no package for this choice.
install.off: Package downloads are switched off by the server setting SARD_AGENT_DOWNLOADS=false, so there are no commands to show here. Install the agent by hand.
install.unsigned: This build of the server hands out unsigned packages, so there is no signature step. Releases of Sard are signed.
install.keyCheck: Compare the key ID and the string with the README.md of the repository before you rely on them. The key comes from this server, so without the comparison the check proves nothing.
install.keyNeeds: The step needs the minisign utility on the host.

download.title: Download the package
download.text: The package, SHA256SUMS and its signature are fetched from this server. The host needs access to this server only.

checksum.title: Check the checksum
checksum.text: Compares the package with its line in SHA256SUMS. Anything but OK means the file is damaged.

signature.title: Check the signature
signature.text: Checks that SHA256SUMS is signed with the Sard release key. Without it the file is only compared with a sum that came from the same server.

install.title: Install the agent
install.text: Installs the package as root. The service is neither enabled nor started: it needs the configuration and a registration first.

configure.title: Create the configuration
configure.text: Copies the example to /etc/sard/agent.yaml, only if there is no such file, and puts this server's address in it. Then open the file and describe your repository: its address and the files with its password and keys stay on the host.

enroll.title: Register the agent
enroll.text: It runs under sudo: the agent itself gives the identity files to the service user sard-agent. The token is shown once, when you create it in Tokens.

repo-add.title: Connect the storage
repo-add.text: The command creates a local restic repository with a generated password and gives the service write access. Save the password outside the host (sudo sard-agent repo password <name> --reveal): without it the backups cannot be restored. S3 and SFTP are connected by the same sudo sard-agent repo add with another address — see the operator docs (agent host setup).

start.title: Start the service
start.text: Enables the service and starts it. The agent connects to the server and appears in the list.

upgrade.title: Update the agent
upgrade.text: Replaces the agent and restic with the new version. The configuration and keys stay as they are.

restart.title: Restart the service
restart.text: Restarts the service only if it is running.

reason.arch_unknown: The agent has not connected yet, so its architecture is unknown and there are no commands. Update it by hand.
reason.arch_unavailable: The release has no package for this agent's architecture. Update it by hand.

upgrade.title: Update the agent
upgrade.available: The server hands out sard-agent {{agent}}, this agent runs an older version.
upgrade.remind: Update when the agent has no active runs: restarting it interrupts them.
upgrade.packageNote: A deb or rpm package replaces the program only: the configuration, keys and the repository password stay as they are.

setup.title: First start
setup.intro: Four things before the console opens: prove you own the server, look at its CA, set the administrator password, and protect the server itself: back it up outside this machine and keep the key copy.

code.title: Setup code
code.hint: The server prints a one-time code in its log when it starts. On the host of the server run:
code.command: docker compose logs server | grep "SARD SETUP CODE"
code.label: Setup code
code.invalid: The code is wrong or has expired. Check it against the log of the server.
code.locked: Too many wrong codes. Try again in {{minutes}} min.

restart.title: A new setup code is needed
restart.message: The setup code has expired or was not issued. Restart the server to get a new one:

setup.completed: The administrator is already set. Sign in.
setup.sessionEnded: The setup session has ended. Enter the setup code from the log of the server again.
setup.unavailable: The server is unavailable. Try again.

ca.title: CA of this server
ca.intro: Agents trust only certificates issued by this CA. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server printed in its log.
ca.keyPath: Key file in the file system of the server
ca.backup: Back up the key separately. Without a copy of the CA key every agent has to be registered again. How: {{doc}}.
ca.replaceSteps: Put the CA files in a directory on the host (for example ./pki-import), create docker-compose.override.yml with the text below and restart the server with docker compose up -d server. Details: {{doc}}.
ca.replaceWarning: After “Use this CA” the CA can no longer be replaced by an import.
ca.migrateOnly: The CA can no longer be replaced by an import. It can be changed only by moving to a new server: {{doc}}.

admin.title: Administrator password
admin.requirements: The password is 12 to 1024 characters long. Use a password manager: it is the only way into the console.
admin.submit: Set the password and open the console

selfBackup.title: Backup of the server itself
selfBackup.intro: Sard backs up its own database, the CA key and the configuration to a storage outside this machine. Until the first backup succeeds, the server accepts no new agents and changes nothing else.

field.hostKeyFingerprint: Fingerprint of the host key, SHA256:… (optional)

selfBackup.noSecrets: No keys or passwords are entered here: the key ID and the secret key are typed in the terminal of the server, and they never reach the browser or the server.

local.warning: A backup on this same machine is lost together with it. I understand that this backup will die with the machine.

command.title: Run on the server
command.hint: Run these lines in a terminal on the machine of the server, in the directory with docker-compose.yml. The last line restarts the built-in agent so that it reports the new repository.
command.verify: Check the command before you run it. It must contain only the "read" line asking for the S3 key ID (for S3), "docker compose run … self-agent repo add" with your own address, bucket and path, and "docker compose restart self-agent". A compromised server cannot vouch for this command itself — you are the one who checks it.
command.label: Commands
command.agentMissing: The built-in agent sard-self is not registered, so there is nothing to add a repository to. See the troubleshooting section: {{doc}}.

wait.title: Waiting for the repository
wait.message: Waiting for the repository from sard-self. When it appears, the wizard binds it itself.
wait.slow: It takes longer than usual. Look at the log of the agent: {{command}}

attach.title: A repository is ready
attach.message: The built-in agent already has the initialised repository {{name}}. Bind the self-backup to it.

selfBackup.bindFailed: The repository could not be bound.

plan.title: What will be backed up
plan.caWarning: The CA key inside the backup is protected only by the password of the repository. Whoever has both the storage and the password has the root of trust of this installation.

schedule.custom: The schedule is {{cron}}. It is not a daily time, so it is shown as it is.
schedule.failed: The schedule could not be saved.

first.intro: The step is done when both the database and the keys have backed up successfully. It cannot be skipped.
first.unavailable: The backup could not be started. Try again.

keys.intro: Restoring needs a recovery key (or the password of this host) and access to the storage. The server holds neither: the key is printed in the terminal once.
keys.storage: Keep the access to the storage as well: the key ID and the secret key of the S3 service, or the SSH key for SFTP.
keys.card: The recovery card says where the storage is and which CA the server has. It holds no password.

keys.unavailable: The server is unavailable. Nothing was confirmed.
keys.pending: The first backup is not done yet.
keys.recoveryCommand: Run this command on the machine of the server in a terminal: it issues a recovery key and prints it once. Keep the key outside this VM:
keys.secondCommand: Or keep the password of this host, printed by this command:

recoveryCard.intro: Keep this card with the copy of the repository password. It holds no password and no keys.
recoveryCard.locationUnknown: not recorded, write it in by hand

recoveryCard.requires: Restoring needs the recovery key (or the password of the host that made the backup) and access to the storage.

onboardingBanner.title: Set up the backup of the server
onboardingBanner.message: The server accepts no new agents until its own backup is set up and the key copy is confirmed.

restore.title: Restore a snapshot
restore.ineligibleTitle: These agents hold the repository but cannot restore from the console

ineligible.agent_outdated: The agent cannot restore from the console: update sard-agent.
ineligible.plugin_missing: The agent has no plugin of the source.

restore.noTargets: No agent can restore this snapshot yet. First attach the repository, with the password from your copy, on the host that should get the data.

warning.agent_offline: The agent is offline: the restore starts when it connects.
warning.owners_not_restored: Files will belong to the agent's service user: owners and groups from the snapshot are not restored. Permissions and modification times are kept.
warning.pg_owners_not_restored: Global objects are not restored: every object of the new database will belong to the connecting role, and access privileges from the snapshot are not carried over.
warning.pg_same_cluster: The database will be restored into the same PostgreSQL cluster the backup was taken from. The restore loads the live cluster: disk and CPU, WAL shipped to replicas and the archive, disk space and locks. A separate cluster is the better target. The server tells this by the agent and the connection address and may miss the same cluster under another address.
warning.globals_change_cluster: Global objects (roles, tablespaces) change the whole PostgreSQL cluster, not just the new database.

blocked.partial: The snapshot is incomplete: it can only be restored on the host with repo restore.
blocked.forgotten: The snapshot was removed from the repository.
blocked.plugin_not_supported: Restoring from the console is not supported for this plugin yet.

restore.ownersNotRestored: Owners and groups from the snapshot were not restored: the files belong to the agent's service user.
restore.nothingRestored: Nothing was restored: the changes were rolled back.
restore.rollbackFailed: Rollback failed, left behind: <m>{{leftover}}</m>. Remove it by hand.
restore.lateSuccess: The agent reported later: the restore succeeded. Data: <m>{{target}}</m>.

banners.noRecoveryKey: Repositories without a recovery key: {{count}}. If the password of their host is lost, the backups cannot be restored.

repositories.command: Command on a host that holds it
